text: And then to address Ms Chong's question about how we will support skill-based HR practices, we have recently introduced tools, like TalentTrack and TalentTrack+, which help employers assess the skills readiness of their workforce and identify suitable training interventions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Gerald Giam also asked how will SWDA coordinate with the economic agencies under the MTI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, WSG and SSG already work closely with MTI and sector agencies through established inter-agency coordination platforms.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With the merger, we will build on these mechanisms to deepen this coordination even further, tightening the nexus between jobs and skills and between enterprise and workforce transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Giam, perhaps it is late in the evening and he may have forgotten, I personally have a stake in this because I am also a Minister in MTI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps I am the political officeholder that he is talking about striding two Ministries because I am also the current Manpower Minister.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, the Member can be assured on this point.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Shawn Loh, Mr Mark Lee, Ms Elysa Chen and Ms Jessica Tan asked whether and how SWDA will work with the trade chambers and associations, industry bodies and sectoral partners.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It will not be limited to these three roles, but they will play three very important roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, as advocates for the manpower needs of their respective sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: TACs and industry bodies will help SWDA to sharpen its workforce development programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Against the backdrop of recent global developments, such as trade tariffs and the Middle East oil crisis, the SNEF and the Singapore Business Federation have provided timely insights on hiring sentiments and business outlook through dipstick business polls.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This helped to inform the Government's policy responses.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, they will serve as key programme partners that will increase the breadth and depth of SWDA's coverage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is our response to Assoc Prof Terence Ho's question about how SWDA will scale impact across the large number of SMEs in different industries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The third point, they will serve as multipliers, amplifying outreach to employers and driving mindset change on workforce transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: SNEF has been co-leading tripartite efforts, such as the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment and the Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development, and can support efforts to engender mindset shifts towards the hiring of senior workers and HR practices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members may be wondering how SWDA's approach to working with partners will be different from before.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: WSG has also partnered on job matching, career guidance and job redesign but these partnerships have been more targeted and scoped.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With SWDA, we will expand and deepen these partnerships to spur new innovations, raise the quality of career and employment services and training.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our initial efforts have begun through pilots under the AfA-ACES and we will continue to build on these.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: SSG works with about 500 training providers, while WSG has only a handful of appointed partners for career matching and guidance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, with this merger, SWDA will broaden this network beyond training providers to include more recruitment agencies, online job portals and other ecosystem players to diversify services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The goal is for workers and employers to have more options and better support, even as we safeguard and uplift the quality of service provision.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving to the fifth group, which is more proactive and more anticipatory support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In a more volatile global environment, the needs of worker and employer segments evolve very rapidly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ms Elysa Chen, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Mark Lee asked how SWDA would play a more proactive and anticipatory role, to prepare workers and businesses ahead of disruptions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Data will be the critical enabler – SWDA will tap on various data sources, including MOM's rich labour market data, demand signals from job postings as well as training take-up.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We can splice and fuse the data in new ways to triangulate and distil fresh jobs as well as provide skills insights.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These insights can then be applied to personalise services and deliver more targeted support proactively.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We seek to leverage these insights to help more individuals enter into good jobs, build careers with better prospects and extend their career trajectories.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I explained earlier, SWDA will also work with the broader career and employment services and training ecosystem to create more value out of shared data, through analysis or building of value-added services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the relationship between SWDA, NTUC and SNEF, and if SWDA will engage them in devising and executing its plans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling called on SWDA to establish regular contact with stakeholders to remain plugged in with ground realities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling spoke about the importance of treating workers as co-creators for AI adoption to ensure better outcomes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ms Eileen Chong spoke about making job redesign a priority when companies integrate AI into their workflows.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Later this evening, depending on what time we end or tomorrow, this House will discuss how we can work together in an era where AI transformation is increasingly pervasive.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I will speak about the importance of concurrent enterprise and workforce transformation in making AI adoption more human-centric.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving on to the sixth point, which is on what measurements of success do we look at.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Several Members indeed asked us, how would we measure SWDA's success?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For individuals, our ultimate goal is to help Singaporeans enter into good jobs and progress in their careers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will measure SWDA's effectiveness in doing so through indicators, such as time to placement and wage growth, in addition to training and placement numbers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We already track these outcome indicators today to measure the effectiveness of our interventions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For employers, we will look at outcomes on adoption of progressive practices in areas, such as job redesign, on-job-training and skills-first hiring.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, to Ms Chong's point, we are tracking such indicators and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will continue to tweak and refine and up the ante.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the economy level, SWDA will contribute to a more inclusive labour market with high resident labour force participation and sustained wage growth.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Median wages have grown over the last decade and we will do our best to extend that growth trajectory.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: While not so easily measured, we also want to engender a culture of lifelong learning and career health to take root in the DNA of the Singapore workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On my last two points, just bear with me.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On the SWDA Board, Mr Saktiandi asked about its composition and the knowledge it will bring.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Sanjeev Tiwari asked whether there will be worker representation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Beyond the Board, we also plan to engage international experts, so that our labour market programmes are informed by global trends and by effective interventions elsewhere.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The composition of the Board will be announced ahead of SWDA's establishment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving on to the last group – transition and continuity.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Specific to Mr Yip Hon Weng's and Assoc Prof Terence Ho's questions on whether MyCareersFuture and MySkillsFuture will be streamlined, we will holistically review the user journey across digital touchpoints to build a more seamless user experience with better signposting to guide users to the appropriate digital services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Yip also asked about how the roles of SSG and WSG employees will change, while Ms Elysa Chen asked how front-line officers will be equipped to adopt a holistic instead of scheme-by-scheme mindset.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will organise SWDA by stakeholder segments so that those at the frontline can provide more holistic support across jobs and skills for their clients.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As SWDA builds a more integrated operating model, roles and structures will evolve.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have identified suitable roles for all officers and we are committed to managing this with care.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will redeploy officers where their experience is most valuable and we will develop those who need new skills to take on new roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our people have been the backbone of SSG's and WSG's achievements.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: SWDA's success will depend on all of them and on bringing them alongside with us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Tan, you have about four minutes left.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you need more than that, the Deputy Leader may want to move an exemption.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think I will need about 10 minutes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In that case, I will just ask Deputy Leader to so move.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: (In Mandarin): Accelerating technological development and the constantly changing international economic environment are making our labour market increasingly complex.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Skills and career development are like rowing against the current – if you do not advance, you will fall behind.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If Singaporeans do not proactively upgrade their skills and plan their careers early, they will inevitably find themselves struggling to keep pace in the labour market and may even miss out on valuable opportunities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If businesses do not keep up with the times and continually innovate, they will inevitably fall behind in market competition.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, Lianhe Zaobao reported that five polytechnics presented the SkillsFuture Lifelong Learning Awards to a total of 15 recipients.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This included two individuals aged over 50 among them – Mr Wang Boyu Peter and Ms Serene Soh Sze-Mei.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: When interviewed, Ms Soh said something that captured the essence of it all: "Age is not an issue.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As long as you are willing to take that first step, you can still embark on a new career." Mr Wang and Ms Soh are role models for lifelong learning.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We can learn from their proactive and determined spirit of self-improvement, as we adapt to the rapidly changing demands of the labour market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Whether you are just entering the workforce, looking to switch careers or hoping to take your career to the next level, we will journey with you.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We hope to work together with every Singaporean to build a sturdy "career-ship" – so that at every stage of your career journey, you can steer its direction with greater confidence and find your own development path amidst changes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: (In English): The formation of SWDA is more than a change in the machinery of our Government.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is a statement of intent – that Singapore will never leave its workers alone in navigating an increasingly complex labour market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That we will build systems worthy of the trust Singaporeans place in them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That we will measure ourselves not by the number of courses run or amount of grants disbursed, but by whether people can find good jobs, grow in their careers and face the future with confidence.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are doing this at a moment of uncertainty.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: AI and technology are reshaping industries faster than we can predict.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The past certainties about career paths and job security are giving way to something significantly more fluid and they are generating more anxiety, more apprehensions for many of us.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But if you look at our history, Singapore has never thrived by waiting for the storm to pass.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The SWDA is one such ship – built to carry our workers and our economy through whatever comes next.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I look forward, I invite all of you to come on board and let us sail together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: After more than five hours and 22 speeches, any clarifications for the Minister?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like — oh, sorry, Mr Kenneth Tiong.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: There is a widespread perception that job postings on MyCareersFuture is a compliance exercise rather than reflects genuine hiring channels.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: So, how would the Minister ensure that more of these MyCareersFuture's postings are genuine vacancies?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Second question, the Minister has not addressed my point on sectoral bargaining.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: The economic skill formation literature is quite clear that firms tend to under-invest in deep skills training when they face poaching risks – they lose the worker, the day after they have spent a lot of time training, putting them through expensive training.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Wage compression through sectoral bargaining is the established solution.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: So, is it the Government's position that NTUC should not bargain at the sectoral level or that sectoral bargaining is unnecessary?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have the exact statistics in terms of what the Member was talking about.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I would ask him to also point me perhaps to the statistics that say that all the advertisements in MyCareersFuture are just a paper exercise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If he can highlight any specific company or instance of companies posting on this particular portal as a paper exercise, we will not hesitate to investigate the company.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But rather than make a blank statement, come up with the specifics.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With regard to poaching risks, I want to also share a different perspective.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Companies that invest in the training of their workers, whether they work through the NTUC Company Training Committees or they work through our job redesign package, work through WSG's Career Conversion Programmes, have seen better retention for their employees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, many of the companies that engage in this type of training tend to attract more talent into their companies against companies who do not.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have been in private sector all my life.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: A certain amount of poaching exists, even amongst doctors, medical professionals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They move from groups to groups, but that does not mean that because of that, the entire industry is, therefore, at risk of being undermined or competed away.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, I can share more of these insights separately.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, inviting Mr Tiong to file a separate Parliamentary Question at another Sitting, given the fact that we have just finished five hours of this debate.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Specifically, will career counsellors move beyond basic resume editing and portal referrals to leverage real time vacancy data for proactive matching and advocate for candidates?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First and foremost, on the jobs and skills that is needed and this will help users to better plan for the upskilling and career needs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: NTUC has its own AI career coach, which, just now, one of the labour Members of Parliament shared.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
text: I am actually really heartened to hear that that MOM is actively tracking the outcomes for individuals who undergo the career conversion programmes, but I also would like to point out that the number of individuals covered by the career conversion programmes are only a small subset of Singaporeans who do undergo many other kinds of career-related training under the SkillsFuture scheme.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
text: So, I would like to ask if the Minister will also like to confirm then that the new agency will indeed also be extending the tracking of these outcomes and whether it is working for these other Singaporeans who are undergoing training, so that Singaporeans can have a clearer picture of what works, what works well, what is not working?

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
text: And I hope the Minister can agree that, by collecting and publicising data like that, that it will only help to further reinforce the importance of lifelong learning and upskilling amongst Singaporeans once they see the numbers for themselves.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have provided just now in my round-up speech about the impact of the career conversion programmes, which is organised by WSG, and I did not add NTUC Company Training Committees' success rates as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Secretary-General will be able to provide that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But suffice to say, to further add on to your other colleague, Mr Giam's earlier point, the SWDA's integrated intelligence function will provide forward-looking signals on what roles and what skillsets are in demand, so then this will allow students and even their families in the IHLs to make more informed decisions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: SWDA will also make the jobs and the skills intelligence accessible through its digital platform, through the multiple career advisory touchpoints.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And guidance is available at the point of decision making, not only after they have entered a particular job itself.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, with that, I believe that that matching should be even more pervasive, and it will reach out to a wider segment of the population.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, we are not just focusing on the workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have also announced at Budget this year, we are enhancing the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package and the grants will tie the companies to specific deliverables with regard to job redesign.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The details will be further shared once SWDA comes into existence in July.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives the Member that reassurance.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am glad to hear that there will be more precise matching with the help of SWDA's the integrated intelligence function.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But can I ask if this function will be provided to all jobseekers who approach SWDA or its agencies, like e2i, to seek for job assistance?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Because it would not be helpful if only a small proportion of jobseekers get to benefit from it, while the rest are just provided with the resume touch-ups or referrals to portals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As long as they go on that Career Health, going on to CareersFinder, SWDA will work with them every step of the way.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Alright, I believe all the clarifications have been addressed.      .
